name: Saypha

lead: Saypha is a portfolio of hyaluronic acid (HA) fillers made by Croma, an Austrian company. Injectors use them to restore or add volume in areas such as the lips, midface and nasolabial folds, which can make the face look fuller or less lined.

Published studies include a randomised lip augmentation trial, a long-term midface study and a systematic review of 947 patients covering the range and its predecessor Princess products. Reported side effects were mostly mild swelling, pain and bruising.

paras: A clinician injects the gel with a needle or cannula in a procedure session, sometimes with a touch-up a few weeks later. Products in the range are named for target areas, such as Saypha LIPS and Saypha VOLUME PLUS, and contain lidocaine for comfort.

A 2026 systematic review found mostly transient swelling, pain and bruising, with one serious treatment-related event across 11 studies and no granulomas or vascular complications reported. Wikipedia describes rare but serious embolic complications as a general risk of fillers.

angle.text: The gel adds volume where it is placed. Studies measure improvements in lip fullness, midface volume and nasolabial fold severity.

lead: Saypha (formerly marketed as Princess) is a range of cross-linked hyaluronic acid dermal fillers made by Croma Pharma of Leobendorf, Austria, using MACRO (MAtrix CROsslinking) technology.[1][2] Different products are intended for lips, midface volume, nasolabial folds and other areas.[2][3][4]

Dermal fillers are used to enhance lips, cheeks and jawline and to correct folds, per Wikipedia.[5] HA fillers are popular because they are temporary and, as the Aesthetic Surgery Journal lip study notes, biocompatible and reversible.[2]
Several trials have tested the range, including a randomised split-face comparison with Juvederm Ultra XC for nasolabial folds and a 36-month midface study.[3][6]

paras: Products in the range target lip augmentation, midface volume deficit and nasolabial folds.[2][3][6]
A postmarket randomised study of Saypha LIPS Lidocaine in 114 patients found more than 90% responders at week 6 on a lip fullness score, with follow-up to 18 months.[2]
A randomised split-face trial compared Princess FILLER Lidocaine (now Saypha filler Lidocaine) with Juvederm Ultra XC for nasolabial folds through up to 48 weeks.[3]
The PRIMAvera study followed 91 patients with midface volume deficit after Princess VOLUME PLUS Lidocaine for up to 36 months.[6]
A small single-site study of 15 women combined Saypha fillers with bespoke skincare.[4]

A 2026 systematic review of 11 studies in 947 patients found that common adverse events were swelling, injection-site pain and bruising, mostly mild to moderate and resolving within two weeks; one severe treatment-related event was reported.[1] Delayed nodules or inflammatory reactions were infrequent and mild, and safety was consistent between Princess and Saypha products.[1]
Wikipedia lists rarer filler complications including infection, allergic reactions, and vision loss from embolism.[5]
